description: Seven living sea turtle species. Depth examples describe particular studies, not species-wide limits. Colours are project design choices.

species.distribution: Atlantic, Pacific and Indian oceans and the Mediterranean; adults commonly use coastal feeding grounds.
species.depth_context: Illustrative surface-to-routine-resting-depth band. Six nesting females at Ascension Island routinely reached 18–20 m on resting dives; deeper resting dives were rare. Not a maximum diving capability or a global typical range.
facts: Adults eat mainly seagrasses and algae.
Feeding and breeding grounds can be separated by long migrations.

species.distribution: Atlantic, Pacific and Indian oceans and the Mediterranean, including coastal and oceanic habitats.
species.depth_context: 26 adult female tracks in the northern Gulf of Mexico spent approximately 80% of their time at 0–30 m. This is a study-specific time-use band, not a species-wide limit.
facts: Strong jaws help crush hard-shelled prey.
Depth use changes with habitat and behaviour.

species.distribution: Oceanic and coastal waters worldwide, extending into cooler feeding regions.
species.depth_context: Post-nesting females tracked from Gabon predominantly occupied the upper 200 m. Deep dives also occurred. This is not a maximum diving capability or a measurement for the demo route.
facts: Its flexible shell differs from the hard shells of other sea turtles.

species.distribution: Tropical Atlantic, Pacific and Indian oceans, often associated with reefs.
species.depth_context: Adult eastern Pacific hawksbills in Gaos et al. spent nearly all their time in the upper 10 m. Other populations use deeper habitats; this is not a universal range.

seasonality.region: Torres Strait and northern Queensland, Australia

facts: A narrow pointed beak helps reach food in reef crevices.
Sponges are an important food source.

species.distribution: Primarily the Gulf of Mexico and northwestern Atlantic; adults commonly use nearshore habitats.
species.depth_context: Bottom-associated behaviour of ONE immature turtle in Gullivan Bay, southwest Florida, occurred in 2–3 m water. This narrow case-study range must not be shown as the typical range for the entire species.
facts: Females can nest together in large groups called arribadas.
This species routinely nests during daylight.

species.distribution: Tropical Atlantic, Pacific and Indian oceans, in coastal and oceanic habitats.
species.depth_context: Range of individual MEAN maximum dive depths in a northern Australia telemetry study, not a minimum-to-maximum range of individual dives. Deepest recorded dive was 200 ± 20 m.
facts: Some populations nest in synchronized arribadas.
Individuals can forage in both shallow and deeper waters.

species.distribution: Northern Australian waters and adjoining waters of Indonesia and Papua New Guinea; all known breeding sites are in Australia.
species.depth_context: Surface-to-study-maximum band for inter-nesting females at Curtis Island, Queensland. The same study recorded a maximum of 44 m at Bare Sand Island. These are local observations, not physiological limits.
facts: Prefers shallow habitats with soft seabeds.
Nesting seasons differ between Australian breeding populations.
